title: Pronouns: Who Is Included?
description: Learn Hawaiian pronouns through repeated sentence frames so you understand who is speaking, who is included, and how many people are involved.

sourceReview.notes: Source check, not educator review. Source spellings are normalized to Unicode ʻokina and NFC. Judd is not used to authorize any live form.

activities.instruction: Start with one person.
activities.prompt: Notice who is doing the action.
activities.support: The sentence stays simple so you can focus on the pronoun.
activities.sentence: E hele au i ke kula.
activities.patternIntro: au means I. One speaker is referring to themself.

parts.label: Action
parts.note: go / will go in this sourced example

activities.languageNote: Do not memorize au as an isolated card only. Listen for what role it plays in the whole sentence.

sourceRefs.section: Nā Papani: Personal, As Subject and After a Preposition

activities.instruction: Now change only who is included.
activities.prompt: Compare this sentence with the previous one.
activities.support: The action and place stay the same. Only the pronoun changes.
activities.sentence: E hele kāua i ke kula.
activities.naturalEnglish: Let's you and me go to school.
activities.patternIntro: kāua means two people: the speaker and the person being addressed.

parts.label: Who
parts.note: you and me — exactly two people

activities.languageNote: The listener is included in kāua.

sourceRefs.section: Nā Papani: Personal, As Subject and After a Preposition

activities.instruction: Contrast inclusive and exclusive 'we'.
activities.prompt: This sentence still refers to two people, but the listener is excluded.
activities.support: Compare māua with kāua.
activities.sentence: E hele māua i ke kula.
activities.naturalEnglish: The two of us, not including you, will go to school.
activities.patternIntro: māua means the speaker plus one other person, excluding the person being addressed.

parts.label: Who
parts.note: two people including the speaker, but not you

activities.languageNote: English says 'we' for both kāua and māua; Hawaiian requires you to track whether the listener is included.

sourceRefs.section: Nā Papani: Personal, As Subject and After a Preposition

activities.instruction: Expand the group.
activities.prompt: Now the group is three or more and includes the listener.
activities.support: Compare kāua and kākou.
activities.sentence: E hele kākou i ke kula.
activities.naturalEnglish: Let's go to school — three or more people, including you.
activities.patternIntro: kākou means the speaker, the listener, and at least one more person.
activities.languageNote: kāua is inclusive dual; kākou is inclusive plural.

sourceRefs.section: Nā Papani: Personal, As Subject and After a Preposition

activities.instruction: Compare the other plural 'we'.
activities.prompt: This group has three or more people but excludes the listener.
activities.support: Compare mākou with kākou.
activities.sentence: E hele mākou i ke kula.
activities.naturalEnglish: We will go to school — three or more people, not including you.
activities.patternIntro: mākou means the speaker and others, but not the person being addressed.
activities.languageNote: kākou includes the listener; mākou excludes the listener.

sourceRefs.section: Nā Papani: Personal, As Subject and After a Preposition

activities.instruction: Track who is included.
activities.prompt: Your friend says: E hele māua i ke kula.
activities.support: Are you included in the group going to school?
options: Yes — the speaker means you and them
No — the speaker means themself and one other person
activities.answer: No — the speaker means themself and one other person
activities.explanation: māua is dual exclusive: two people including the speaker, excluding the listener.

sourceRefs.section: Nā Papani: Personal, As Subject and After a Preposition

activities.instruction: Track the listener.
activities.prompt: Someone tells you: E hele kākou i ke kula.
activities.support: Which interpretation is correct?
activities.explanation: kākou is plural inclusive: three or more people including the listener.

sourceRefs.section: Nā Papani: Personal, As Subject and After a Preposition

activities.instruction: Track how many people.
activities.prompt: E hele kāua i ke kula.
activities.support: How many people does kāua refer to here?
activities.explanation: kāua is first-person dual inclusive: you and me.

sourceRefs.section: Nā Papani: Personal, As Subject and After a Preposition

activities.instruction: Track how many people.
activities.prompt: E hele mākou i ke kula.
activities.support: How many people does mākou refer to?
activities.explanation: mākou is first-person plural exclusive: three or more including the speaker, excluding the listener.

sourceRefs.section: Nā Papani: Personal, As Subject and After a Preposition

activities.instruction: Now listen for second person number.
activities.prompt: The action stays familiar; only the listener group changes.
activities.support: This is a question directed to exactly two people.
activities.sentence: Ua hele ʻolua i ke kula?
activities.naturalEnglish: Did you two go to school?
activities.languageNote: Hawaiian distinguishes one listener, two listeners, and three-or-more listeners.

sourceRefs.section: Nā Papani: Personal, As Subject and After a Preposition

activities.instruction: Expand the listener group.
activities.prompt: Compare ʻolua with ʻoukou.
activities.support: This question is addressed to three or more people.
activities.sentence: Ua hele ʻoukou i ke kula?
activities.naturalEnglish: Did you, three or more people, go to school?
activities.patternIntro: ʻoukou means you, when addressing three or more people.
activities.languageNote: English 'you' hides number; Hawaiian does not.

sourceRefs.section: Nā Papani: Personal, As Subject and After a Preposition

activities.answer: E hele au me ʻoukou i ke kula.
activities.explanation: The addressed group has three or more people.

activities.instruction: Recall the taught Hawaiian form for this meaning.
activities.prompt: I will go to school.
activities.support: Use the model from this lesson; the check is not a judge of all possible translations.
activities.answer: E hele au i ke kula.
activities.model: E hele au i ke kula.

sourceRefs.section: Nā Papani: Personal, As Subject and After a Preposition

activities.explanation: Do not memorize au as an isolated card only. Listen for what role it plays in the whole sentence.

activities.instruction: Recall the taught Hawaiian form for this meaning.
activities.prompt: Let's you and me go to school.
activities.support: Use the model from this lesson; the check is not a judge of all possible translations.
activities.answer: E hele kāua i ke kula.
activities.model: E hele kāua i ke kula.

sourceRefs.section: Nā Papani: Personal, As Subject and After a Preposition

activities.explanation: The listener is included in kāua.

activities.instruction: Recall the taught Hawaiian form for this meaning.
activities.prompt: The two of us, not including you, will go to school.
activities.support: Use the model from this lesson; the check is not a judge of all possible translations.
activities.answer: E hele māua i ke kula.
activities.model: E hele māua i ke kula.

sourceRefs.section: Nā Papani: Personal, As Subject and After a Preposition

activities.explanation: English says 'we' for both kāua and māua; Hawaiian requires you to track whether the listener is included.

activities.instruction: Recall the taught Hawaiian form for this meaning.
activities.prompt: Let's go to school — three or more people, including you.
activities.support: Use the model from this lesson; the check is not a judge of all possible translations.
activities.answer: E hele kākou i ke kula.
activities.model: E hele kākou i ke kula.

sourceRefs.section: Nā Papani: Personal, As Subject and After a Preposition

activities.explanation: kāua is inclusive dual; kākou is inclusive plural.

activities.instruction: Recall the taught Hawaiian form for this meaning.
activities.prompt: We will go to school — three or more people, not including you.
activities.support: Use the model from this lesson; the check is not a judge of all possible translations.
activities.answer: E hele mākou i ke kula.
activities.model: E hele mākou i ke kula.

sourceRefs.section: Nā Papani: Personal, As Subject and After a Preposition

activities.explanation: kākou includes the listener; mākou excludes the listener.

activities.instruction: Recall the taught Hawaiian form for this meaning.
activities.prompt: Did you two go to school?
activities.support: Use the model from this lesson; the check is not a judge of all possible translations.
activities.answer: Ua hele ʻolua i ke kula?
activities.model: Ua hele ʻolua i ke kula?

activities.explanation: Hawaiian distinguishes one listener, two listeners, and three-or-more listeners.
